question: What five characteristics should an effective traffic control device have under Section 1D.01?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Under Section 1D.01, an effective traffic control device should have five characteristics: it should fulfill a need, command attention, convey a clear and simple meaning, command respect from road users, and give adequate time for proper response. These are Guidance (recommended) provisions, and the Manual adds that design, placement, operation, maintenance, and uniformity should be carefully considered to maximize consistency with these five principles. Guidance (recommended): - "To be effective, a traffic control device should: A. Fulfill a need; B. Command attention; C. Convey a clear, simple meaning; D. Command respect from road users; and E. Give adequate time for proper response." - Design, placement, operation, maintenance, and uniformity should be carefully considered in order to maximize the ability of a traffic control device to be consistent with the five principles; vehicle speed and road-user types should be carefully considered as an element governing design, operation, placement, and location of devices. - The proper use of traffic control devices should provide the road user with the information necessary to safely, efficiently, and lawfully use the streets, highways, pedestrian facilities, and bikeways. - Placement of a device should be within the road user's view so adequate visibility is provided, appropriately positioned with respect to the location, object, or situation to which it applies, with location and legibility such that the road user has adequate time to respond in both day and night conditions (this operationalizes the "adequate time for proper response" principle). - Traffic control devices should be placed and operated in a uniform and consistent manner as part of maintaining uniformity in traffic control. - When developing messages for changeable message signs, Section 1D.01 should be consulted for the principles of an effective traffic control device. Visual evidence: - [Image 5] shows the printed text of Section 1D.01, including the Guidance paragraph listing the five characteristics (A through E) of an effective traffic control device. - [Image 6] shows Section 1D.09, whose placement and uniformity guidance supports the "adequate time for proper response" and "command respect" principles. - [Image 1], [Image 2], [Image 3], [Image 4], [Image 7], and [Image 8] depict signal assemblies, sight distance tables, mounting heights, signal face arrangements, and other sections not directly relevant to the five principles in Section 1D.01. Citations: - Section 1D.01 Guidance §3 (p.31) - Section 1D.01 Guidance §4 (p.31) - Section 1D.01 Guidance §5 (p.31) - Section 1D.09 Guidance §3 (p.38) - Section 1D.09 Guidance §4 (p.38) - Section 2L.04 Guidance §3 (p.513) - Page 72 - Page 79
gold_answer: It should fulfill a need, command attention, convey a clear and simple meaning, command respect from road users, and give adequate time for proper response.
